title: Hollister 1031 Exchange Coordination
name: Hollister 1031 Exchange Coordination
metaTitle: Hollister 1031 Exchange Coordination | San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Hollister ag-support industrial near the airport, San Benito Street retail, and a growing Highway 25 commuter market.

sections.html: Hollister sits in San Benito County, a step removed from the dense Silicon Valley build-out but connected to it more each year as Highway 25 commuters move into the area looking for housing they can no longer find closer to San Jose. Commercial real estate here still runs smaller than in Santa Clara County, small industrial and ag-support buildings near the municipal airport, downtown retail along San Benito Street, and multi-tenant buildings sized for a market only beginning to feel commuter-driven growth pressure. San Benito County's agricultural roots remain visible throughout the surrounding area even as the county seat itself takes on more of a bedroom-community character, and a buyer should expect that dual identity to persist for years rather than assume Hollister will convert quickly into a fully built-out suburban market.

sections.heading: Small Industrial and Ag-Support Buildings Near the Airport
sections.html: Industrial buildings clustered near the Hollister Municipal Airport serve a mix of agricultural support businesses and small manufacturers, and building quality varies more widely here than in a more built-out industrial market, some structures are decades old with limited modern infrastructure, while others have been updated to serve newer tenants. A replacement property buyer should walk the specific building rather than relying on a listing description alone, since two buildings of similar square footage in this corridor can differ substantially in condition and remaining useful life. Proximity to the airport itself can also carry use restrictions or noise-easement considerations on certain parcels, and a buyer should confirm these directly with the county rather than assuming a standard industrial zoning designation covers every detail relevant to the site.

sections.heading: Highway 25 and the Commuter Bedroom Community Shift
sections.html: Highway 25 has become the primary route for Hollister residents commuting north toward Gilroy and the broader Silicon Valley job market, and that commuter growth has started to pull retail and service demand into Hollister that did not exist in the same volume a decade ago. A buyer identifying Hollister replacement property tied to this shift should review population growth and rooftop delivery data for the surrounding area, since retail demand here is still catching up to residential growth rather than fully mature.

sections.heading: Downtown San Benito Street Retail
sections.html:
San Benito Street carries Hollister's small downtown retail corridor, serving longtime residents alongside the newer commuter population moving into the area. A diligence file for a San Benito Street property typically includes:

  • Trailing rent roll and tenant turnover history
  • Building condition assessment given the wide range of construction eras in this corridor
  • Water and wastewater capacity documentation for any ag-support industrial use
  • Population growth and rooftop delivery data supporting retail demand claims
  • Airport proximity and any applicable use restrictions for nearby parcels
  • Phase I environmental site assessment

A buyer should not assume retail rents here will match Gilroy or South San Jose comparables, since Hollister's retail base is still smaller and less mature despite the growing commuter population.

sections.heading: Rent Roll Analysis for Small Multi-Tenant Buildings
sections.html: Small multi-tenant industrial and retail buildings in Hollister often carry a mix of long-established local tenants and newer businesses responding to the area's growth, and a rent roll analysis should separate these two groups clearly, since legacy tenants may be paying below-market rent that will not carry forward at renewal. A buyer should model both the current stabilized income and a realistic post-renewal projection rather than relying on the current rent roll as a permanent baseline.

sections.heading: Reverse Exchange Coordination When Timing Runs Backward
sections.html: Because Hollister inventory can be thin for a specific building type, some exchangers use a reverse exchange, acquiring the replacement property before closing on the relinquished property, when they find a Hollister building they do not want to lose while still marketing their existing asset. A qualified intermediary or exchange accommodation titleholder must hold the replacement property during this structure, and the relinquished-property sale must still close within the applicable exchange period. This content describes process and coordination only; an exchanger should confirm the specific reverse exchange structure with a tax advisor before proceeding.

faqs.q: Why does building condition vary so much among Hollister industrial properties?
faqs.a: Many buildings near the municipal airport are decades old with limited modern infrastructure, while others have been updated for newer tenants, so a buyer should walk the specific building rather than relying on square footage or a listing description alone.

faqs.q: Is Hollister retail demand fully mature or still growing?
faqs.a: Still growing. Highway 25 commuter growth has pulled retail demand into Hollister that did not exist at the same volume a decade ago, and retail delivery is still catching up to that residential growth rather than fully stabilized.

faqs.q: Should I expect Hollister retail rents to match Gilroy comparables?
faqs.a: No. Hollister's retail base is smaller and less mature than Gilroy's despite the growing commuter population, so rent comparisons should be drawn carefully rather than assumed to track a neighboring market.

faqs.q: What should I check on a Hollister rent roll with long-established tenants?
faqs.a: Separate legacy tenants from newer ones, since long-established tenants may be paying below-market rent that will not carry forward at renewal, and model both current and realistic post-renewal income.

faqs.q: When would a reverse exchange make sense for a Hollister purchase?
faqs.a: If a buyer finds a specific Hollister building they do not want to lose while still marketing their existing property for sale, a reverse exchange lets a qualified intermediary or accommodation titleholder acquire the replacement property first, provided the relinquished-property sale still closes within the applicable exchange period.
